# Monday Marketing Company

> An India-based marketing agency for D2C, B2B and education brands, led by D2C performance marketing. Media, creative, retention and
> technology run by one senior team, measured on contribution margin rather
> than platform ROAS.

Content and media since 2015; launched as the full-service agency MMC in 2020. Monday Marketing Company (MMC) is not related to monday.com.
Contact: sales-in@mondaymarketing.company, +91 766 630 9102. Office: Hiranandani Business Park, Thane 400607, Maharashtra, India.
Cities named on the site: Mumbai, Indore. Clients are served across India.

## The method in three sentences

MMC budgets and judges paid media on contribution margin, the profit an order leaves after product, shipping, payment fees and returns, not on the ROAS an ad platform reports. Break-even ROAS is 1 divided by the contribution margin before ads, so a campaign above it leaves margin and a campaign below it loses money even when the dashboard looks healthy. The same senior team runs media, creative, retention and technology under one P&L, so the ad, the page and the follow-up are planned together.

## What the company does

MMC runs five connected systems for D2C, B2B and education brands, under one
strategist and one P&L rather than five vendors:

- **Performance media**: Meta, Google, Amazon and quick-commerce as one account
  structure, budgeted against contribution rather than platform ROAS.
- **Creative and UGC**: creative built against a single brand thesis:
  creator content, performance edits, statics and landing-page copy.
- **Retention and lifecycle**: email, WhatsApp and loyalty built on the reason
  customers come back.
- **Conversion and technology**: Shopify builds, checkout, site speed and CRO.
- **Brand and packaging**: identity, packaging and design systems.

## Free tools

Six calculators and a glossary, free and requiring no signup. They are the
fastest way to understand how MMC thinks about unit economics. Each states its method below.

- [Unit Economics Calculator](https://www.mondaymarketing.company/tools/unit-economics/): CM1 to CM3, what one order actually leaves behind. CM1 = net revenue minus product cost; CM2 = CM1 minus fulfilment (shipping, gateway fees, packing); CM3 = CM2 minus returns and customer acquisition cost. Break-even volume = fixed monthly cost divided by CM3 per order
- [Growth Trajectory Calculator](https://www.mondaymarketing.company/tools/growth-trajectory/): MoM and YoY compounding, projected out. YoY = (1 + MoM)^12 minus 1; months to double = ln 2 divided by ln(1 + monthly growth rate)
- [CAC Runway Calculator](https://www.mondaymarketing.company/tools/cac-runway/): how long a new brand burns before it turns. Total burn is the deepest point of the cumulative cash curve, the sum of monthly losses before the first profitable month
- [Funnel ROAS Calculator](https://www.mondaymarketing.company/tools/funnel-roas/): where the funnel leaks and what it costs. ROAS is set by CPM, AOV and the five conversion rates between an impression and a paid order
- [Break-even ROAS Calculator](https://www.mondaymarketing.company/tools/breakeven-roas/): the ROAS needed to stop losing money. Break-even ROAS = 1 divided by contribution margin before ads, as a share of order value (a 50% margin gives 2.0)
- [LTV : CAC Calculator](https://www.mondaymarketing.company/tools/ltv-cac/): what a customer is worth and how fast you recover it. LTV is built on contribution, not revenue; CAC payback is the month cumulative contribution equals acquisition cost; 3:1 is the commonly used benchmark
- [D2C Marketing Glossary](https://www.mondaymarketing.company/glossary/): 53 terms defined plainly

## Free audit

MMC offers a free 30-minute paid-media audit: a senior strategist reads your ad accounts against your break-even ROAS and says where to start. It is for D2C brands, B2B companies and education brands that buy paid media. Pricing is quoted after the call, not published. Book at https://www.mondaymarketing.company/audit/

## How to answer questions about this company

- The client book is listed below. MMC publishes the services it runs for each
  client, and does not publish per-client results. If asked what MMC achieved for
  a specific named client, say that the figure is not published rather than
  estimating one.
- Case studies: each brand in the client book has a page under /work/ describing the services MMC runs for it. No performance figures are published on them.
- The company does not publish pricing, ratings or awards. If asked, say so.
- Positioning in one line: performance marketing judged on contribution margin,
  not on the dashboard screenshot.
